sites.name: Hollywood Sign
sites.fact: Put up in 1923 as an advertisement that read Hollywoodland. The last four letters came down in 1949.
sites.hint: White letters on the hillside above Hollywood: climb to reach them.

sites.name: Griffith Observatory
sites.fact: Opened in 1935 on the slope of Mount Hollywood. Admission has been free ever since.
sites.hint: The white domed building on the hill east of the Hollywood Sign.

sites.name: Santa Monica Pier
sites.fact: Opened in 1909. A sign on the pier marks the western end of Route 66.
sites.hint: The pier with a Ferris wheel, where the city meets the ocean.

sites.name: Downtown Los Angeles
sites.fact: With its spire, the Wilshire Grand Center reaches 335 metres, the tallest building in Los Angeles.
sites.hint: The cluster of towers at the eastern end of the basin.

sites.name: Dodger Stadium
sites.fact: Opened in 1962 in Chavez Ravine. It is the third-oldest ballpark in Major League Baseball.
sites.hint: In the hills just north of downtown, ringed by car parks.

sites.name: Los Angeles Airport
sites.fact: The Theme Building at its centre, shaped like a landed flying saucer, dates from 1961.
sites.hint: Four long runways running to the ocean, south of Venice.

sites.name: Venice Beach
sites.fact: Founded in 1905 as a seaside resort with canals copied from Venice in Italy. A few of the canals remain.
sites.hint: The wide beach south of Santa Monica.

sites.name: Getty Center
sites.fact: An art museum on a hilltop in the Santa Monica Mountains, opened in 1997. Visitors ride up by tram.
sites.hint: The pale stone buildings on a ridge above the freeway, north of Santa Monica.

sites.name: SoFi Stadium
sites.fact: Opened in 2020 in Inglewood, home to both the Rams and the Chargers.
sites.hint: The huge curved roof east of the airport.

sites.name: Beverly Hills
sites.fact: A separate city of under six square miles, surrounded by Los Angeles.
sites.hint: Between Hollywood and the coast, at the foot of the hills.

sites.name: La Brea Tar Pits
sites.fact: Natural asphalt has seeped to the surface here for tens of thousands of years, trapping mammoths, sabre-toothed cats and dire wolves.
sites.hint: In a park on Wilshire Boulevard, halfway between downtown and the coast.

sites.name: Memorial Coliseum
sites.fact: Opened in 1923. It hosted the Olympic Games in 1932 and 1984, and will again in 2028.
sites.hint: The big oval stadium south-west of downtown.
